reason: The rack's branding makes ownership uncertain, so I'll check the purchase book before changing its controls.
expectation: I expect to identify which rack equipment the cooperative owns, though the records may not settle everything.

alternatives.reason: Preparing local fobs seems useful, but establishing ownership first seems more prudent.

effect: The receipts establish that the cooperative owns the controller, wiring and switches, but not the modem.
reaction: The distinction behind the oversized sticker is satisfying.
reason: I'll compare the migration notice with the identified equipment to understand what needs local control.
expectation: I expect the notice to clarify which services or controls are affected, though it may not specify every component.

alternatives.reason: Preparing fobs could support local access, but I want to understand the affected equipment first.

effect: The modem's approval lead is isolated, so its permission signal can no longer control the door; the uplink remains available.
reaction: I didn't expect the notice comparison to include physically disconnecting the lead.
reason: Connect the local controller to the rack to establish a replacement control route.
expectation: I expect the cooperative's controller to gain local control of the rack, though it may need further configuration.

alternatives.reason: The fobs may provide access later, but the controller connection seems necessary first.

effect: The cooperative's equipment now responds locally using its existing fallback settings, without consulting an account server.
reaction: It's satisfying to see the local connection work, though access still needs attention.
reason: Preparing the service fobs is the only offered combination and may provide local access.
expectation: I expect the controller to configure the fobs for local use, though they may still need to be paired with the rack.

effect: The residents now have fobs enrolled on their own controller, with a spare set in the repair kit.
reaction: It's reassuring that neither the company nor Moth controls those permissions.
reason: The selector is the only offered combination and may let residents use their fobs for local control.
expectation: I expect the fobs to be paired with the selector, though further setup may be needed.

effect: The selector recognizes the residents' fobs, but someone must still operate its handle.
reaction: The distinction between authorization and actually moving the switch is clear.
reason: The only offered combination should make the selector easier to identify by touch.
expectation: I expect the raised strips to label the selector, though it may still need to be operated or installed.

effect: The selector now has raised LOCAL and EXTERNAL labels that Miro can identify by touch.
reaction: Miro's eyes-shut check makes the accessibility improvement concrete.
reason: The only offered combination should connect the marked selector to the locally addressed rack.
expectation: I expect the selector to provide a way to choose local control, though someone may still need to operate it.

effect: The installed selector works with both residents' fobs, completing the move to shared local control.
reaction: It's satisfying that control no longer depends on June's toolbox alone.

mostWorthwhile.text: Checking the purchase book was most worthwhile: it turned the intimidating branding into a concrete distinction between the leased modem and cooperative-owned equipment.

leastWorthwhile.text: Enrolling the fobs and pairing them with the selector felt somewhat procedural, especially with only one combination offered at each step.

surprise.text: Comparing the notice with the rack also removed the modem's approval lead; I hadn't expected that comparison to include a physical disconnection.

arbitrary.text: The notice-to-lead removal felt abrupt: the purpose was clear afterward, but the offered combination did not make the physical action obvious beforehand.

continue.text: I would continue: the ownership distinction and shared-control payoff made me curious how the neighborhood will extend its independence, though the later one-option steps were less engaging.
